qd56b3f85.question: Acceptance criteria (the Story carries none; derived from the ISSUE's fix intent, c1-c7): ac1 a full index keeps the summary of every document still stored with the same body, under its new entity number, and drops the rest; ac2 a full index interrupted after the delete loses no summary, and the next full index writes the carried ones back; ac3 docSummary.restoreFromBackup restores the backup's summaries for every document whose current body has the same content hash, by either model, never replaces a stored summary and is idempotent; ac4 writeDocSummaryIfCurrent without options and the summariser's skip rule are unchanged, and the summariser's error placeholder never replaces a stored summary with no errorCode for the same contentHash.
qd56b3f85.rationale: Stakeholder decision 2026-10-18: ac1-ac4 as stated; the approved LLD's test mapping already maps every proving test to them.

q6880ca99.question: cd1 partial: restoreCarriedDocSummaries, writeDocSummaryIfCurrentInTxn, markFullIndexUnfinished, restoreDocSummariesFromBackup (the store-level function behind the IPC handler) and the IPC method docSummary.restoreFromBackup are new names; there is no HLD to own them (standalone fix).
q6880ca99.rationale: Stakeholder decision 2026-10-18: the standalone S001 LLD is the authority for the four store functions and the docSummary.restoreFromBackup IPC method; its section 2 already gives their signatures, behaviour and errors.

summary.prose: A full index no longer throws away document summaries. In the same transaction that deletes the repository's rows, every summary is moved into a carry table keyed by the document's stable string id; once the rebuild has stored the documents again, each carried summary is written back only if its document still exists with the same content hash, and its carry row is removed in that same transaction, so a full index that is interrupted keeps its summaries for the full index start-up queues next. A one-time daemon IPC method reads the 2026-10-16 backup read-only and restores its summaries the same way, never overwriting a summary the live store already holds.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: LLD for ISSUE-dced43851723554f: keep document summaries across a full index (a summary whose document is still stored with the same content hash after the rebuild survives, re-keyed to the document's new entity number), and a one-time daemon-side restore of summaries from the schema-v4 backup of 2026-10-16 for every document whose current body has the same content hash.

api.name: deleteEntitiesForRepo
api.signature: deleteEntitiesForRepo(db: DbClient, repo: string, opts?: { readonly returnIncomingToPending?: boolean | undefined; readonly carryDocSummaries?: boolean | undefined }): Promise<{ returnedToPending: number; carriedDocSummaries: number }>

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: The repository whose rows are deleted.

parameters.name: opts.carryDocSummaries
parameters.purpose: When true, every doc_summary row of the repository's entities is copied into doc_summary_carry inside the delete's own write transaction (the existing `before` hook of detachDeleteEntities), before the per-entity cascade removes it; with no entities there is nothing to carry and existing carry rows are kept. When false or absent, the repository's carry rows are deleted in a write transaction of deleteEntitiesForRepo's own that runs whether or not the repository has entities (detachDeleteEntities returns before its hook when the entity list is empty, src/db/entities.ts:1104), so repo.remove after an interrupted full index leaves nothing behind.

returns.meaning: carriedDocSummaries is the number of summaries copied into the carry by this call (0 without the option).

errors.condition: A failure inside the delete transaction rolls back the delete and the carry together; nothing is lost.

preconditions: The repository is registered (an unregistered repository returns { returnedToPending: 0, carriedDocSummaries: 0 } as today).
postconditions: With carryDocSummaries: for every summary deleted from doc_summary for this repository there is a doc_summary_carry row with the same DocSummary under (repoId, the entity's string id); a carry row already present from an interrupted full index is kept (a doc_summary row for the same id overwrites it, being newer).
Without it: the repository has no doc_summary_carry rows.
deleteDocSummariesForRepo still runs; its per-repository sweep is unchanged.

api.name: writeDocSummaryIfCurrent
api.signature: writeDocSummaryIfCurrent(db: DbClient, entityId: string, repo: string, summary: DocSummary, opts?: { readonly keepGoodSummary?: boolean | undefined }): Promise<DocSummaryWriteOutcome | 'kept-good'>  // without opts unchanged; its body is factored into writeDocSummaryIfCurrentInTxn(s: GraphStore, entityId: string, summary: DocSummary, opts?: { readonly onlyIfAbsent?: boolean | undefined; readonly keepGoodSummary?: boolean | undefined }): DocSummaryWriteOutcome | 'already-present' | 'kept-good'

parameters.name: s
parameters.purpose: The caller's write transaction (in-txn variant only).

parameters.name: summary
parameters.purpose: The summary to write; its contentHash is checked against sha256 of the stored body.

parameters.name: opts.onlyIfAbsent
parameters.purpose: When true, a document that already has a doc_summary row is left as it is ('already-present'). Used by the backup restore so a live summary is never replaced by an older one.

parameters.name: opts.keepGoodSummary
parameters.purpose: When true, a stored summary with no errorCode and the same contentHash as the one being written is left as it is ('kept-good'), checked inside the write transaction. Passed by summariseDoc for its error placeholder (src/analyze/summariser/driver.ts:238-240), so a summary restored or written back while the model was running is never replaced by a placeholder when the model fails.

returns.meaning: 'written', 'entity-gone', 'body-changed' as today; 'already-present' only with onlyIfAbsent; 'kept-good' only with keepGoodSummary. The in-txn variant takes the repository id from the stored entity row, not from a caller-supplied path.

errors.condition: The public function keeps its current throw for an unregistered repo.

preconditions: Called inside a write transaction (in-txn variant).
postconditions: Without opts the public function behaves exactly as before for its callers; the summariser's successful write (src/analyze/summariser/driver.ts:278) passes no option, so a fresh summary still replaces whatever is stored. The public function is declared with two overloads, so the no-options call keeps its exact return type: writeDocSummaryIfCurrent(db, entityId, repo, summary): Promise<DocSummaryWriteOutcome> and writeDocSummaryIfCurrent(db, entityId, repo, summary, opts: { readonly keepGoodSummary: true }): Promise<DocSummaryWriteOutcome | 'kept-good'>; the successful-write branch at src/analyze/summariser/driver.ts:278-281 compiles unchanged. In the placeholder branch (src/analyze/summariser/driver.ts:240-242) summariseDoc returns { ok: false, skipped: 'kept-good', errorCode, errorMessage } for 'kept-good': SummariseDocResult.skipped (src/analyze/summariser/driver.ts:157) gains 'kept-good', documented as 'the model failed but a good summary of the same body was stored meanwhile and kept'. The sweep's classification (src/indexer/doc-summary-sweep.ts:56-58) counts it as skipped through its existing `res.skipped !== undefined` branch, unchanged.

api.name: restoreCarriedDocSummaries
api.signature: restoreCarriedDocSummaries(repo: string): Promise<{ written: number; entityGone: number; bodyChanged: number }>

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: The repository whose carry rows are written back.

returns.type: { written: number; entityGone: number; bodyChanged: number }
returns.meaning: How many carried summaries were written back and how many were dropped because the document is gone or its body changed.

errors.condition: A failed batch transaction leaves that batch's carry rows in place for the next full index.

preconditions: Called by fullIndex after the index clean-up (reconcileRepo) and before finishFullIndexState, so every document the rebuild stores is stored.
postconditions: Each carry row is removed in the same write transaction as its write-back (batches of 500 rows per transaction), so a row is never both lost and uncarried.
The repository has no doc_summary_carry rows when it returns.

api.name: docSummary.restoreFromBackup
api.signature: IPC 'docSummary.restoreFromBackup' (params: { backupPath: string }) => Promise<{ read: number; written: number; alreadyPresent: number; entityGone: number; bodyChanged: number; undecodable: number }>

parameters.name: backupPath
parameters.purpose: Absolute path of a single-file LMDB store (noSubdir) holding doc_summary and entity_string_by_u64, e.g. /Users/subhagho/.insrc/backup/graph.lmdb.schema-v4.2026-10-16T16-59-39-955Z.

returns.type: { read; written; alreadyPresent; entityGone; bodyChanged; undecodable }
returns.meaning: Counts over every doc_summary row of the backup: written to the live store, skipped because the live store already holds a summary for the document, skipped because the document is not stored or its body changed, or skipped because the row or its id mapping could not be read.

errors.condition: backupPath is missing, not absolute, not a file, or is the live store's own path.
The backup cannot be opened read-only or lacks the doc_summary or entity_string_by_u64 database.

preconditions: The daemon owns the live store; the backup is opened as a separate read-only environment and closed when the call returns.
postconditions: The backup file is not modified.

Every write goes through writeDocSummaryIfCurrentInTxn with onlyIfAbsent: true, in batches of 500 rows per write transaction; summaries by the previous model are written as they are (the summariser's model rule replaces them in time).
Running it twice writes nothing the second time (every row is then alreadyPresent, entityGone or bodyChanged).

dataModelChanges.details: Key: repoId u32 big-endian || UTF-8 string entity id. Value: encodeDocSummary(summary), the same encoding as doc_summary. Written only by deleteEntitiesForRepo({ carryDocSummaries: true }); read and removed by restoreCarriedDocSummaries; removed for a repository by deleteEntitiesForRepo without the option. Opened in openGraphStore beside doc_summary through open_ (an empty database on first open), so the v5 layout and SCHEMA_VERSION are unchanged.

fullIndex first writes fullIndexFinished = false for the repository (a new markFullIndexUnfinished(repoPath) in src/db/index-state.ts that sets only that flag) BEFORE deleteEntitiesForRepo, so a crash at any point after the delete leaves the repository unfinished and start-up queues a full index (src/indexer/index.ts:261-267); beginFullIndexState stays where it is and keeps its counter reset. It then passes carryDocSummaries: true to deleteEntitiesForRepo and calls restoreCarriedDocSummaries(repoPath) after the index clean-up and before finishFullIndexState; the comment that says the summaries are regenerated is corrected. This closes a window the Epic c2ba6fa6 s1 rebuild already had (deleteEntitiesForRepo and deleteUnresolvedForRepo run before beginFullIndexState), which the carry depends on. The doc-summarise-repo job is still queued at the end and now skips every written-back document (same contentHash and model).

errorCases.scenario: The full index is interrupted (daemon stop, crash, a thrown pass) after the delete and before restoreCarriedDocSummaries.
errorCases.detection: fullIndexFinished is false from markFullIndexUnfinished, written before the delete (so the window before beginFullIndexState is covered too), and start-up queues a full index again; the carry rows of the repository are still in doc_summary_carry.
errorCases.response: The re-queued full index deletes again with carryDocSummaries (the repository now has few or no doc_summary rows, so little is added) and its restoreCarriedDocSummaries writes back every carried row, the ones from the interrupted run included.
errorCases.userImpact: None: the summaries come back when the next full index finishes.

errorCases.scenario: A write-back batch transaction fails inside restoreCarriedDocSummaries.
errorCases.detection: withWriteTxn throws; the error propagates out of fullIndex like any indexing failure, so the repository's status is 'error' and fullIndexFinished stays false.
errorCases.response: The failed batch's carry rows are rolled back with it and stay carried; earlier batches are written and removed. The next full index writes back the rest.
errorCases.userImpact: The repository reads not complete until the next full index; no summary is lost.

errorCases.scenario: docSummary.restoreFromBackup is given a path that is missing, not absolute, not a regular file, or the live store's own file.
errorCases.detection: The handler checks isAbsolute, statSync().isFile() and compares realpath against the live graph store path before opening anything.
errorCases.response: Reject the call with an Error naming the reason; nothing is opened or written.
errorCases.userImpact: A clear error; the store is untouched.

errorCases.scenario: The backup opens but lacks doc_summary or entity_string_by_u64, or cannot be opened read-only.
errorCases.detection: open() with readOnly: true throws, or the named database is not present in the backup's main database listing.
errorCases.response: Close the backup environment and reject with an Error; nothing is written.
errorCases.userImpact: A clear error; the store is untouched.

errorCases.scenario: A backup row's value cannot be decoded by decodeDocSummary, or its u64 has no entity_string_by_u64 mapping in the backup.
errorCases.detection: decodeDocSummary throws, or the mapping lookup returns undefined.
errorCases.response: Skip the row and count it as undecodable; continue with the rest.
errorCases.userImpact: That one summary is regenerated by the sweep in time.

errorCases.scenario: A carried or backup summary's document is no longer stored, or its body changed.
errorCases.detection: writeDocSummaryIfCurrentInTxn finds no entity_id_by_string entry or entity row ('entity-gone'), or sha256(body) differs from summary.contentHash ('body-changed').
errorCases.response: Do not write it; a carry row is removed in the same transaction; the outcome is counted.
errorCases.userImpact: None: the summary would be wrong for the current body; the sweep summarises the document afresh.

errorCases.scenario: The summariser's model call fails for a document whose summary was restored or written back while the model was running.
errorCases.detection: summariseDoc's catch block (src/analyze/summariser/driver.ts:232-240) writes its placeholder with keepGoodSummary; inside the write transaction the stored row has no errorCode and the same contentHash.
errorCases.response: The placeholder is not written ('kept-good'); the good summary stays.
errorCases.userImpact: None: the document keeps its summary instead of an error row.

edgeCases.input: A repository with no summaries is fully indexed.
edgeCases.expected: carriedDocSummaries 0; restoreCarriedDocSummaries returns all zeros; behaviour as today.

edgeCases.input: A full index of a repository after an interrupted one, where the live doc_summary holds a summary for an id that is also carried.
edgeCases.expected: The doc_summary row overwrites the carry row in the delete transaction (it is the newer one); one write-back.

edgeCases.input: repo.remove of a repository that has carry rows (an interrupted full index, then removal).
edgeCases.expected: deleteEntitiesForRepo without the option deletes that repository's carry rows; none remain.

edgeCases.input: A carried summary whose document is stored by the rebuild under the same string id but a new entity number.
edgeCases.expected: Written back under the new number with a doc_summary_by_repo entry; the sweep then skips the document when the summary's model is the configured one.

edgeCases.input: docSummary.restoreFromBackup while a full index of that repository is running.
edgeCases.expected: A document not yet stored is 'entity-gone' (not written); a document whose live summary was already written back is 'already-present'. Run again after the index finishes to restore the rest; the call is idempotent.

edgeCases.input: docSummary.restoreFromBackup while the summary sweep runs.
edgeCases.expected: Write transactions are serialised by LMDB. The restore never replaces a summary the sweep wrote (onlyIfAbsent). If the restore lands while the model is running on that document: a successful model call replaces it with a fresh summary of the same body (correct); a failed one writes its error placeholder with keepGoodSummary, so the restored summary is kept ('kept-good'). A restored current-model summary makes the sweep skip that document when it reaches it later.

edgeCases.input: A backup summary written by the previous model (qwen3.6:35b-a3b).
edgeCases.expected: Restored as it is; the summariser regenerates it when the sweep reaches it, and readers have a summary meanwhile.
written 0; every row is alreadyPresent, entityGone, bodyChanged or undecodable.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Every summary written by the summariser's conditional path, the carry write-back and the backup restore is stored only for a document whose stored body hashes to the summary's contentHash, checked inside the write transaction (writeDocSummaryIfCurrent, Story b94cf2c9). The unconditional writeDocSummary keeps its current behaviour for its existing callers and tests (src/db/__tests__/doc-summaries-lmdb.test.ts).
The summariser's skip rule is unchanged: same contentHash, same modelId, no errorCode means skip; anything else is summarised.
A full index still deletes every entity row of the repository and rebuilds it from scratch (Epic c2ba6fa6 s1); only the summaries are carried, and they are re-keyed to the new entity numbers.
The per-entity summary cascade (deleteDocSummaryInTxn) and the per-repository sweep (deleteDocSummariesForRepo) still run; doc_summary never holds a row for an entity number that is not stored.
The daemon alone writes the store: the restore runs inside the daemon over IPC and opens the backup as a separate read-only environment.

migration.stateBefore: A full index deletes every summary of the repository: the per-entity cascade deleteDocSummaryInTxn (src/db/entities.ts:1139) and the repository sweep deleteDocSummariesForRepo (src/db/entities.ts:601-602), called from fullIndex at src/indexer/index.ts:617; summaries are keyed by the entity number, which the rebuild reassigns, and the doc-summarise-repo sweep regenerates each at about 35 s. The live store (schema v5) holds no summaries for the six repositories after the reindex of 2026-10-18; the 2026-10-16 schema-v4 backup holds 22,216.
migration.stateAfter: The store has a doc_summary_carry database; a full index carries the repository's summaries through the rebuild and writes back each one whose document is unchanged, so the sweep only summarises changed or new documents. The live store's lost summaries are restored from the backup for every document whose current body has the same content hash.

migrationSteps.action: Ship the code: the GraphStore opens the new doc_summary_carry database on the next daemon start (an empty named database; SCHEMA_VERSION stays 5, no layout step). Update the installed daemon with the maintenance update and restart it.

Run docSummary.restoreFromBackup once over IPC with /Users/subhagho/.insrc/backup/graph.lmdb.schema-v4.2026-10-16T16-59-39-955Z after every repository's full index has finished (repo.list completeness), and record the counts in the smoke evidence. The call writes only summaries whose document has no summary now and whose body matches; it can be run again safely.
Reindex this repository once and record that the summary count after the reindex equals the count before it less the documents that changed or were deleted (the carry works end to end).

migration.backwardCompat: deleteEntitiesForRepo keeps its signature with one more optional option and one more field in its result ({ returnedToPending, carriedDocSummaries }); its two other callers (repo.remove in src/daemon/index.ts:576 and src/db/repos.ts:192) pass no option and behave as before, now also clearing the repository's carry rows. The existing test src/db/__tests__/entities-return-to-pending.test.ts asserts the exact result ({ returnedToPending: 1 } and { returnedToPending: 0 }); both expectations gain carriedDocSummaries: 0, its pending-edge assertions unchanged. writeDocSummaryIfCurrent is unchanged for its callers. The new IPC method is additive; no IDE plugin calls it. An older daemon build opening a store that has doc_summary_carry ignores the extra named database.

alternativesConsidered.name: In-memory snapshot and conditional rewrite, plus a restore IPC
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: fullIndex reads the repository's (entityId, summary) pairs before the delete and rewrites each through writeDocSummaryIfCurrent once the files are indexed; a daemon IPC method restores from a backup file the same way.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add listDocSummaryPairsForRepo(db, repo) to src/db/doc-summaries.ts (zipping listDocSummariesForRepo with listDocSummaryEntityIdsForRepo inside one read). In fullIndex (src/indexer/index.ts) call it before deleteEntitiesForRepo, hold the pairs in memory, and after the file walk (before the summary job is queued at :758) call writeDocSummaryIfCurrent for each pair, counting written / entity-gone / body-changed. For the lost summaries add a daemon IPC method docSummary.restoreFromBackup { backupPath } that opens the backup LMDB file read-only, walks doc_summary, maps each u64 to its string id through entity_string_by_u64, takes the repository from the live entity row and calls writeDocSummaryIfCurrent; it skips a row whose live summary is already current. No storage layout change.
pros: Smallest change; reuses the existing conditional write, so a summary is never attached to a changed body
No schema change (the live store is v5; a layout change needs a v6 step)
The restore and the carry-forward share one write path and one test seam
cons: The snapshot lives only in memory: a full index interrupted between the delete and the rewrite loses the repository's summaries again (start-up re-queues the full index with nothing to carry)
Holds every summary of the repository in memory during the index (about 11k rows for this repository, a few MB)
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Smallest, but the in-memory snapshot repeats the defect on any interrupted full index, which a full index of a large repository (hours) makes likely.

alternativesConsidered.name: Durable carry table written in the delete transaction, plus a restore IPC
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: deleteEntitiesForRepo moves the repository's summaries, keyed by string entity id, into a doc_summary_carry sub-DB in the same transaction as the delete; fullIndex rewrites them conditionally after the walk and clears the carry; the restore IPC is as in a1.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a doc_summary_carry sub-DB (string entity id -> DocSummary, plus the repository) opened beside doc_summary, and an option { carryDocSummaries: true } on deleteEntitiesForRepo that, inside its write transaction, copies each summary it deletes into the carry. fullIndex passes the option, and after the file walk rewrites every carried row of the repository through writeDocSummaryIfCurrent and deletes it from the carry (in the same transaction as the write). A full index interrupted part-way leaves the carry in place; the re-queued full index at start-up appends nothing new (the summaries are already gone from doc_summary) and rewrites the carried rows when it finishes. The restore IPC is the a1 method. Adding a sub-DB is additive (an empty sub-DB on open), but a new named database in a v5 store must be checked against the schema-version rule.
pros: Survives an interrupted full index: no summary is lost between the delete and the rewrite
The delete and the carry are one transaction, so there is no window where a summary exists in neither place
Same conditional write as a1, so correctness of the attach is unchanged
cons: A new sub-DB in the store and its clean-up rules (repo.remove must clear the carry)
May need a schema-version step if the store's version rule treats a new named database as a layout change
More code than a1 and a second place a summary can live

alternativesConsidered.name: Key summaries by string entity id so the delete need not touch them
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Change doc_summary's key from the entity u64 to the deterministic string id, and stop the full index deleting summaries; a stale summary is skipped by the existing contentHash check.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Re-key doc_summary and doc_summary_by_repo by the string id (a v6 layout step migrating every row), drop the deleteDocSummaryInTxn and deleteDocSummariesForRepo calls from the full-index path, and rely on the summariser's contentHash rule plus a sweep that removes summaries whose entity is not stored after a full index. The restore copies backup rows straight into the new layout when the body hash matches.
pros: No snapshot at all: a summary is independent of the entity number, so every future rebuild keeps it by construction
cons: A v6 schema migration of the live store and every reader of doc_summary
Orphan summaries of deleted documents need a new clean-up pass
Much larger change than the defect needs
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Robust by construction but needs a v6 layout migration and an orphan pass, far beyond the defect.

erDefinition.narrative: Where a document summary lives during a full index: in doc_summary under the entity number before the delete, in doc_summary_carry under the stable string id between the delete and the write-back, and in doc_summary again under the new entity number after it.

DocSummaryRow.description: A row of doc_summary, keyed by the entity's internal number, which a full index reassigns.

summary.description: The DocSummary, including contentHash and modelId.

DocSummaryCarryRow.description: A row of the new doc_summary_carry database, holding a summary across a full index under the document's deterministic string id.

repoId.description: The repository's registry id (stable across a reindex); the key's prefix.

entityId.description: The document's deterministic string id (SHA256 of repo, file, kind, name); the key's suffix.

summary.description: The carried DocSummary, written back only if the document's body still hashes to its contentHash.

contentHash.description: sha256 of the document body the summary was made from.

modelId.description: The model that wrote it; the summariser regenerates a summary by another model.

a2 is the only alternative scoring 'satisfies' on every constraint: it keeps fix-intent 1 across an interrupted full index (a1 scores only 'partial' there) and needs no layout change (a3 'violates' the v5 store). Accuracy is primary, so the extra sub-DB is worth it.
